title: LinkedIn 的 HashMap resize 凍結——調查一場記憶體預算失算
summary: 排除 CPU throttle、kernel compaction、Envoy、RocksDB 四個假設後，off-CPU profile 揭穿 FishDB 的 10 秒凍結來自 hashbrown 在 58.7M 條目時觸發 3.5 GB mmap、整個 process 被 mmap_lock 寫鎖凍住。
widget_questions: How does the size of the next HashMap doubling allocation — and the resulting mmap_lock write-hold cost — scale with the current live key count, and where on that curve does the 58.7M freeze point fall?

Which of the four conventional culprits (CPU throttling, kernel memory compaction, Envoy sidecar, RocksDB mmap I/O) were ruled out, what evidence falsified each, and which surviving candidate did off-CPU profiling confirm?

What three distinct kernel-side off-CPU stack shapes did eBPF offcputime expose during the freeze — who held the mmap_lock write rights, who queued on read-mode for madvise, who queued on read-mode for page-fault?

If you pre-allocate the HashMap with base_index × k entries up-front, how far does the next doubling threshold move, and how many years of organic growth does that buy at 2–3 million entries per shard per day?

What does the temporal sequence of the mmap_lock chain look like — who acquires the write rights, when do other threads enqueue on the read slow-path, and what fraction of the freeze window is spent waiting versus mmap-ing?

Looking at the five candidate hypotheses side-by-side, how does the evidence weight that ruled each one out (or confirmed the survivor) compare — was the rule-out cheap and decisive, or did it require cross-layer trace alignment?

What does the canonical RSS sawtooth from repeated HashMap doublings look like — how big is the transient spike, how much permanent step does each event leave, and how would a rolling-window alert catch it before users notice?
